analysis.title: Worst Since COVID: Morgan Stanley Sifts Through A Record 70% Tech Momentum Crash, Rock-Bottom Hedge Fund Nets And "Deep Fear"
key_insights: Nasdaq 100 fell 6.4% and SOX fell 12.2% on Thursday after Wednesday's 1.6% S&P 500 gain. After a modest Friday bounce the S&P 500 finished the week down 2.7% and the Nasdaq 100 down 4.9%.

The US TMT Momentum pair is down 70% from June highs, its largest one-year drawdown on record. Two weeks earlier it was down 62%. The Global Risk Demand Index reached -3.4SD, its lowest in over a year.

The Nasdaq 100's 6.4% drop was its worst day since March 2020 and the 31st worst in 40 years. The Nasdaq VIX hit its highest level since Liberation Day. Thursday was the biggest put day in Cboe history.
The SOX's 12.2% fall was its second-worst day on record, behind only March 2020. Semis now trade on a single-digit two-year forward P/E for the first time in five years.
On days when QQQ rose and the MS AI basket (MSXXAI) fell, the spread reached -7.2pp, more than three times worse than any underperformance in the past two years.

The trigger was the midterms. Goldman sees Democratic state-level wins leading to moratoria that could freeze about 45% of planned US data center capacity. Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa said the state should stop its data center build-out until new protections are in place. Georgia, Ohio and Michigan are reported to be lining up to copy Texas.

Stephen Byrd notes ERCOT's interconnection queue is ~474GW, more than 5x Texas's peak demand, and warns US data center capacity may be insufficient by 2028. He sees Cipher Mining, Galaxy Digital and Solaris facing uncertainty in Texas. He sees Williams, Equinix, Digital Realty and Bloom Energy ahead because their power is already secured.

MS Prime Brokerage: Thursday was the 5th largest single-day drop in US L/S net leverage since 2010. Net leverage fell 8 points on the week to 42% (8th percentile since 2010, 0th percentile over the past year). Gross fell 4 points to 202%, a 12-month low, after ~10.7% cumulative de-grossing of global GMV since June.
AI is ~32% of US funds' net exposure, down from 47% at the June peak. About 40% of US L/S funds are flat or down for the year. Tech hedge funds wiped out their entire 2026 gain on Thursday.
Bull backtest: when net leverage has been in the bottom decile, forward S&P returns averaged 6.3% over three months and 20.7% over twelve, vs. 3.1% and 12.7% across all deciles.

Bear backtest from MS QDS: when SPX falls more than 2.5% and MSZZMOMO falls more than 3.5% on the same day, the S&P averaged roughly -1.5% one and three weeks later and -1% after a month. After extreme levered ETF rebalancing supply, bounces have typically come within three weeks. McElligott counted a $165 billion mechanical purge on Thursday.

Single-name volatility across the S&P is in the 99th percentile vs. five years, up 16 percentiles in a week. One-month US return dispersion is in the 99th percentile of its 20-year range, matching Covid-era levels and exceeded meaningfully only in the GFC. European dispersion is the highest since March 2022.
Q3 S&P 500 profit growth is tracking 31.4% with 84% of companies beating, but the average beat is only 2.7%. Earnings revisions breadth fell to +10% from a +26% peak.

Palantir posted its 13th straight quarter of accelerating revenue growth (96% YoY) and the stock did not rally. Shopify fell sharply despite 30% constant-currency GMV growth. Cloudflare (revenue growth 39% vs 36%) and Airbnb (16% room-night growth vs ~12% expected) were exceptions. Savone says FCF surprises are driving larger stock reactions than EPS surprises and the debate has moved to AI spending in 2028.

MS's Joyce Jiang finds 16% of software leveraged loans are classified as high risk from AI disruption, and nearly three-quarters of that bucket is rated B- or CCC. Credit has not reacted as stocks have.

Macro held up better than sentiment: October payrolls were 165K vs 70K expected, unemployment fell to 4.1%, and the US economic surprise index hit a three-year high. Michael Gapen estimates AI spending added 0.9pp to annualized 3Q GDP, still sees $1.6 trillion of hyperscaler capex in 2027, and expects two 25bp Fed hikes in December and March.
Markets price fewer than two hikes through end-2027, down from 3-4 a month ago. Savone says the Fed may be in less of a hurry than investors would prefer.

Mike Wilson thinks the correction that began in June is in its final innings and keeps an 8,000 S&P year-end target. He wants either further capitulation or a move to 7,100-7,300 before adding risk more aggressively. His Fresh Money Buy List now includes Delta, Knight-Swift, Northrop Grumman, EQT and Target.
Asia: KOSPI 200 fell 6.5% and an early 8%+ drop in the broader KOSPI triggered a circuit breaker. Nikkei fell 6.0% and Hang Seng fell 1.3%.

European semis fell more than 8% Thursday vs. a 30bp dip in European software. Semis now trade at a 19% P/E discount to software vs. a 116% premium at their highs. MS's Lee Simpson sees the 7% ASML drop as overdone.
Brent fell nearly 20% in three sessions through Wednesday, its biggest weekly drop since the Covid crash. MS's Martijn Rats sees $75 Brent by 4Q27. Hedge funds sold $6.6 billion of Brent.
MS's Takeshi Yamaguchi warns persistent equity volatility could push the BoJ's December hike into January.

Counterpoint from the author: the four prior 6%+ Nasdaq drops over 15 years were followed by gains above 25% in three months. Three came in March 2020 with Fed easing and one on April 4, 2025, days before the tariff pause. The author argues no comparable policy support is present now and expects the bounce to be short covering.

tension_points.bull_case: Net leverage at 42% is in the bottom decile of its history. Forward S&P returns in such cases averaged 6.3% over three months and 20.7% over twelve. Prior 6%+ Nasdaq drops were followed by gains above 25% in three months. Wilson sees the correction in its final innings.
tension_points.bear_case: MS QDS finds the S&P kept falling, averaging about -1.5% after one and three weeks, when the market and momentum factor both fell hard on the same day. The prior 6%+ drops came with Fed easing or a tariff pause, and none is available now with the Fed expected to hike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Wilson wants further capitulation or a move to 7,100-7,300 on the S&P before adding risk more aggressively. Next week's CPI is the next test for the bounce.

tension_points.bull_case: Names with power already secured (Williams, Equinix, Digital Realty, Bloom Energy) come out ahead. Behind-the-meter power avoids dependence on the grid.
tension_points.bear_case: Goldman sees state moratoria freezing about 45% of planned US data center capacity. Texas-exposed Cipher Mining, Galaxy Digital and Solaris face uncertainty.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Other states such as Georgia, Ohio and Michigan following Texas would widen the risk.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets price fewer than two hikes through end-2027, down from 3-4 a month ago, which supports risk assets.
tension_points.bear_case: Gapen still expects two 25bp hikes in December and March. Payrolls beat by 95K and euro area inflation is at 4%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Next week's CPI is the next hurdle for the rate path.
